title: The Cave That Breathes with the Tide

segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Find an easy position and let the breath arrive as it is. One hand may rest on the belly and one on the chest.
[soft, slow, warm voice] On an inhale, invite gentle movement beneath the lower hand. On the exhale, let the belly settle without pushing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [gentle waves lapping] Imagine the lower ribs as a cave beside the sea. Water enters quietly and the walls make a little space.
[soft, slow, warm voice] The tide leaves in its own time. Keep every breath smaller than strain.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice expansion toward the front, sides, and back... a three-dimensional room rather than a balloon forced outward.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let several breaths follow their own tide with no counting.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] If you feel dizzy, tingly, or uncomfortable, return to ordinary breathing immediately.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Try a soft count only if it helps: in one... two... three... out one... two... three.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Release the count and listen for the quiet point between waves, without holding the breath there.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Allow shoulders, throat, and jaw to remain unhelpfully relaxed while the diaphragm does less dramatic work.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let the hands grow light and trust the body to continue breathing.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Leave the cave beside the tide. Feel the room and breathe however feels natural now.
